stem.text: Why is the second ionisation energy of sodium larger than the second ionisation energy of magnesium?

A.text: The attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron is greater in $\text{Na}^{+}$ than in $\text{Mg}^{+}$.

B.text: The nuclear charge of $\text{Na}^{+}$ is greater than that of $\text{Mg}^{+}$.

C.text: The outer electron of $\text{Na}^{+}$ is more shielded than the outer electron of $\text{Mg}^{+}$.

D.text: The outer electron of Na is in the same orbital as the outer electron of Mg.
